This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a problem in a game. Then it explains the idea behind it. It ends
with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. The full explanations,
examples and exercises are in the notes.

## Key terms

{{< glossary media-channel art-style sound-effect ambience feedback diegetic player-experience >}}

## 2.1 The media inventory

- Step 1: describe, do not judge yet.
- Make an **inventory**: a table of all media elements, with their channel.
- Five **media channels**: visual (the **art style**, characters, effects),
  audio (music, **sound effects**, voices, **ambience**), text and story,
  cinematic (cut-scenes, trailers), interface (menus, HUD).
- The inventory is complete when everything the player sees or hears has a
  row.

![An annotated screen of Ember Trail.](images/annotated-screen.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Inventory of your game"}
Take a screenshot of one busy moment in a game you play. Make a table:
element, channel, when it appears. Write at least six rows. Keep it for the
next tasks.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Which channel?"}
Choose the media channel.

::: {.match}
The soft, round shapes of all the characters.
:   visual

The sound of wind in the forest.
:   audio

The speech bubble "The bridge is out!".
:   text and story

A short film between two chapters.
:   cinematic

The health bar and the coin counter.
:   interface
:::
:::

## 2.2 The functions of media

- Every element has a job (a **function**).
- **Feedback**: what happened because of my action?
- **Guidance**: where should I go?
- **Mood**: how should this moment feel?
- **Story**: what is happening?
- **Identity**: which game is this?
- One element can have several functions.

![One coin, three functions: mood, feedback and guidance.](images/media-functions.png){width=94%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
"There is music in the menu" only describes. Say what the element does to the
player: "the slow flute music makes the player calm before play".
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The jobs of your media"}
Choose three elements from your inventory. For each one, write its function
and one sentence about its effect on the player.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Which function?"}
Choose the main function.

::: {.match}
A chime and a flash when the player collects a coin.
:   feedback

A glowing door at the end of a dark corridor.
:   guidance

Slow strings and rain sounds in a sad scene.
:   mood

An old statue that shows how the village was destroyed.
:   story

A short theme tune that players know from the first second.
:   identity
:::
:::

## 2.3 Inside or outside the game world

- **Diegetic**: inside the game world; the characters could notice it
  (a campfire's crackling, footsteps).
- **Non-diegetic**: only for the player (background music, the score).
- **Spatial**: placed in the world, but not part of the story (a name above
  a character).
- **Meta**: part of the story, but not placed in the world (red marks on the
  screen when the hero is hurt).
- Diegetic = more immersion, but slower to read. Non-diegetic = clear and fast.

![Four kinds of interface elements.](images/diegesis.png){width=78%}

{{< sim file="sims/sound-stage.html" poster="sims/sound-stage.png" title="Sound Stage: inside or outside the world?" kind="game" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Sound Stage"}
Walk the fox past the campfire in **Sound Stage** and switch the layers on and
off. Which sounds change when the fox moves? Which stay the same? Make two
lists: diegetic and non-diegetic.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Diegetic or not?"}
Choose the right answer. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match}
The fox's footsteps.
:   diegetic

The flute music of Ember Trail.
:   non-diegetic

The coin counter in the corner.
:   non-diegetic

A name floating above another character.
:   spatial

The screen turns red at the edges when the fox is hurt.
:   meta

A radio that plays in a car that the player drives.
:   diegetic
:::
:::

## Game challenge: analysing Ember Trail {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

*Ember Trail* is a 2D adventure game for phones. A young fox crosses a forest
at night to go home. The art style is soft and round, the colours are warm
against deep blue, and the music is a solo flute with wind sounds. The
interface shows health, coins and a pause button. A speech bubble says "The
bridge is out!", coins lie along the safe path, and short animated scenes
between chapters tell the story.
Play the media hunt first: it uses the same screen.

{{< sim file="sims/ember-trail.html" poster="sims/ember-trail.png" title="Ember Trail: media hunt" kind="game" height="600" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Your analysis (harder)"}
Ember Trail: a fox, a campfire, flute music, coins along the safe path, a
"+10" and a "ting" for each coin, scenes between chapters. Choose the right
answer.

::: {.match extra="non-diegetic|mood"}
The crackling of the campfire as the fox walks past it.
:   diegetic

The coins lie along the safe path. Main function?
:   guidance

The "ting" and "+10" of a coin: main function?
:   feedback

The animated scenes between chapters: main function?
:   story

The flute theme that players know at once: main function?
:   identity
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- Inventory first: every element, by channel.
- Five functions: feedback, guidance, mood, story, identity.
- Diegetic = inside the world; non-diegetic = only for the player.
- Explain each element by its job and its effect on the player.
